rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a flow ends when one condition holds, and that under a second, alternative condition the flow returns to an earlier ongoing activity that keeps delivering new items, so the two outcomes would be reunited before the flow ends: Model the ending outcome as its own branch that leads directly to an end event. Model the returning outcome as a sequence flow back to the earlier ongoing activity. If the two outcomes are reunited by a merge gateway, the merged path must still have a route to an end event: give the returning path its own decision that can lead to an end event, or do not merge it into the ending path at all. Verify that every merge gateway has an outgoing route to an end event.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description has nested threshold conditions on one quantity, where each lower threshold triggers an additional action, and the branches of these conditions are reunited by a merge gateway

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that when a supplier cannot deliver the full amount of an item, the remaining amount must be ordered from several other suppliers, and otherwise the order continues with one supplier, so a sufficiency check follows the placement of the orders: After the orders are placed, model an exclusive gateway whose question asks whether the chosen supplier covers the full required amount. Give one labelled outgoing flow for 'enough' that continues to the next step, and one for 'not enough' that leads to a task ordering the remaining amount from several other suppliers. Merge the flows back with an exclusive merge gateway before the parallel gateway that starts the work. Do not omit the check or route all orders straight to the start of the work.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that when a supplier cannot deliver the full amount of an item, the remaining amount must be ordered from several other suppliers, and otherwise the order continues with one supplier, so a sufficiency check follows the placement of the orders

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a sequence of threshold checks on one quantity (each check compares the quantity to a different level and triggers a different follow-up action), and it also states a separate action for the case where the quantity is fully exhausted, so that case is an additional outcome of the same checks: Model the threshold checks as successive exclusive gateways, in the order the description gives them, each with one labelled outgoing flow per outcome. Attach each threshold outcome to the follow-up action the description gives for it. Add an outgoing flow from the relevant check for the fully-exhausted outcome, and attach it to a task for the action the description gives for that case. Do not treat the exhausted case as covered by the lower-threshold branch, and do not drop it as an exception.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a condition on a quantity that changes as deliveries or other events arrive (for example, a count of items still needed or a level that falls over time), and it says that a follow-up action, a repetition, or a further wait follows depending on whether that condition holds: Model an exclusive gateway at the point in the flow where the condition is checked, placed after the event or activity that changes the quantity and before the step the condition controls. Label it with the condition in the description's wording and give it one labelled outgoing flow per outcome. Route the outcome that repeats or continues waiting back through an exclusive merge to the earlier step. Do not fold the check into the arrival event or the preceding activity, and do not omit the gateway because the next step seems to follow anyway.
